question: Prediction of conversion from MCI to AD within about 3 years among ADNI-1 MCI patients. The shared channel is structural MRI: P-179 combines baseline FreeSurfer ROI volumes with blood SNP and mRNA data; P-186 combines MRI morphometry with neuropsychological measures. Input representation differs (one baseline visit vs two observed visits plus a forecast third value), which the rule treats as a candidate explanation, not a disqualifier.

figures.P-186: Linear SVM on three-point trajectories (two observed visits + forecast value), MCIp = conversion before month 36, ADNI-1, 5-fold CV; no intervals. 1-year-ahead, NM+MRI, 9 markers, 35 MCIp / 50 MCIs: AUC 0.957; Hanley-McNeil Q1=0.957/1.043=0.918, Q2=2*0.9158/1.957=0.936, SE=sqrt([0.957*0.043+34*(0.918-0.9158)+49*(0.936-0.9158)]/(35*50))=0.025 -> 0.908-1.000. 6-month-ahead, NM+MRI, 49/70: 0.912 (SE 0.030 -> 0.854-0.970). MRI only: 1-year 0.905 (SE 0.037 -> 0.833-0.977); 6-month 0.88 (SE 0.034 -> 0.813-0.947). Ground-truth benchmark with actual third readings (not the method's figure): 0.98 (NM+MRI, 1-year).

matched_figure_check: Neither paper reports the other's input condition: P-186 has no single-baseline-visit arm and P-179 no longitudinal arm, so no fully matched figure exists. The closest is P-186's MRI-only arm, which removes P-186's non-shared channel (still longitudinal). It narrows the gap and sits at the edge of the rule's test: 6-month MRI-only 0.88 (0.813-0.947) and P-179's 0.826 (0.746-0.906) each lie inside the other's interval; 1-year MRI-only 0.905 (0.833-0.977) excludes 0.826 by 0.007 while 0.905 lies inside P-179's interval (upper bound 0.906); combined difference z = 0.079/sqrt(0.041^2+0.037^2) = 1.45. The recorded headline pair, 0.957 (0.908-1.000) vs 0.826 (0.746-0.906), excludes each other both ways (z = 2.75).
performance_validity: Passes the Section 3.5 test as written: P-186's 0.957 is below 0.97 (internal 5-fold CV, n=85, no external cohort); its 0.98 is the ground-truth benchmark, not the method's figure. P-179's 0.826 passes.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation and timing: P-186 scores trajectories that include readings after baseline and a forecast value, which its authors say drives the 0.957; P-179 uses one baseline visit. The attribution is asserted, not shown with a baseline-only arm.
candidate_explanations.quote: Te method proposed in this paper has recorded the highest classi\ufb01cation AUC of 95.7% predominantly because of involving the forecasted marker value at the time of conversion as a classi\ufb01cation feature.

candidate_explanations.difference: Non-shared predictors: neuropsychological measures (ADAS, RAVLT) in P-186 versus blood SNP and mRNA in P-179; P-186's MRI-only arm is 0.905/0.88 against 0.957/0.912 with NM added.
Eligible population and sample: ADNI-1 MCI with three complete consecutive readings (85 or 119 subjects) versus 125 ADNI-1 MCI with baseline blood omics.
candidate_explanations.quote: for 1-year-ahead prediction, the dataset contains three consecutive annual readings, resulting in 35 MCIp and 50 MCIs subjects.

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation design: P-186 normalises before the train-test split, ranks markers by t-tests on baseline readings without stating that this happens inside the folds, and reports the marker-subset size with the best AUC.
candidate_explanations.quote: We scale all features to have values between 0 and 1 before the train-test split.

candidate_explanations.difference: Outcome window: P-186 counts conversion any time before month 36, which for early converters overlaps the observed readings; P-179 counts conversion within three years of baseline.
candidate_explanations.quote: converting to AD any time before the last follow-up time, i.e., 36th month, are called MCI progressors (MCIp)

reason: Same question (ADNI-1 MCI-to-AD conversion within about 3 years, MRI shared), same metric, and the recorded AUCs, 0.957 and 0.826, exclude each other's intervals; neither is near ceiling and neither paper reports the other's single-visit or longitudinal condition. But on the shared MRI channel P-186's own figures (0.88 at 6 months, 0.905 at 1 year) come within or to the edge of P-179's uncertainty, so whether the papers' data dissolve the gap depends on treating P-186's still-longitudinal MRI-only arm as the matched figure. The candidate explanations, chiefly the forecast value at the time of conversion, are not shown to be sufficient.
